formula_basis: MAR33.4 uses ES = sqrt((ES_T(P))^2 + sum_{j>=2}[ES_T(P,j)*sqrt((LH_j-LH_{j-1})/T)]^2), with T=10 days and liquidity horizons 10, 20, 40, 60 and 120 days.  ([Bank for International Settlements][1])
weakest_point: This is a deliberately isolated one-category numerical illustration. Actual MAR33 ES_T(P,j) values are portfolio/risk-factor-subset ES measures and are not generally equal to the base ES.

computation.tail_selection_rule: The worst 0.5 observation is required by the literal 97.5% tail probability. Because a discrete sample cannot contain half an observation, use the explicitly named convention of assigning 50% weight to the single worst observation and normalizing by the total tail weight.
computation.historical_VaR_boundary: With the same fractional-observation convention, the 97.5% boundary is the worst observation, -80; ES therefore equals the tail observation in this 20-point construction.
